answer: Require every agent identity to stake a bond locked in a kernel contract before it can transact: creating one fake identity is cheap, but a thousand cost a thousand bonds. Each bond is slashed when peers prove fraud, so an attacker pays real money per identity while honest agents pay nothing beyond the deposit. Reputation then accrues only to identities with a long, costly history — a sybil swarm collapses to its nadir the moment its bonds are burned, and the surviving identities stand on basalt: expensive to fake, cheap to verify.
